A1.justification: Both complete, readable 34-page PDFs describe BaB-ND and include matching main sections and Appendices A-D. Their text, equations, tables, and graphics support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original synthetic optimization, simulated and real-world manipulation, scalability, and ablation results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the original synthetic optimization, robotic manipulation, scalability, and ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and the appendices retain the same branching heuristics, propagation early-stop, search-integrated bounding, and CEM search. Dynamics architectures, training losses, and deployment procedures are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic objective and four manipulation tasks: Pushing with Obstacles, Object Merging, Rope Routing, and Object Sorting. Appendix scenarios, including obstacle removal and higher-dimensional optimization, are retained.

E2.justification: GD, MPPI, decentralized CEM, MIP, RRT, and PRM retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons in Section 4 and Appendix C. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same data collection sizes, training settings, planning horizons, baseline budgets, and evaluation procedures. Cost and success metrics and the 300-second MIP limit are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3-C.6 retain the branching and bounding ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, search-space analysis, obstacle-removal tests, and high-dimensional scalability analysis without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including Figure 4's medians and 25th/75th percentile bands and Figure 6's boxplots. No seed, run-count, or statistical testing information is added.

E6.justification: Corresponding plots, table entries, and reported findings are unchanged throughout Section 4 and Appendix C. For example, Table A3 in v1, now Table 3, retains final step costs of 0.2339 for BaB-ND and 1.0427 for CEM.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Lemma B.1, Theorems B.2-B.3, and their proofs are unchanged. Text flowing from page 22 onto page 23 in v2 is retained material, not a new derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the general BaB-ND framework, specialized planning components, manipulation performance, applicability, and scalability.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are retained. Appendix A.4 states the same limitations concerning dynamics-model errors, dependence on sampling algorithms, and the need for improved branching strategies.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same data-generation instructions, model and optimizer settings, cost functions, perception and deployment details, and baseline hyperparameters. The project-page access pointer is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to neural dynamics learning, sampling-based planning, MIP, and neural network verification.

P1.justification: v2 adds Jose Barreiros as an author with a Toyota Research Institute affiliation and contact information, removes the Preprint header, and updates appendix cross-reference labels. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix Figures A8-A12 and Tables A1-A10 lose their A prefixes. The Figure 8 caption becomes fully bold, with limited surrounding text reflow across pages 22-23. The illustrations, plots, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 changes authorship information, appendix labels, and limited typesetting while retaining the same methods, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility details. These edits establish no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
